ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure has four small schematic diagrams arranged horizontally, labeled ①, ②, ③, and ④ respectively; each small diagram has a gray horizontal band representing a pressure belt, and wind-direction arrows beside it representing a wind belt. The latitude labels of ① and ③ are 30°, and the latitude labels of ② and ④ are 60°. From the wind-direction arrows in the figure, ② and ④ are one group of pressure belts and wind belts near 60°, and ① and ③ are one group of pressure belts and wind belts near 30°. Then reason: To determine the Northern and Southern Hemispheres, look at the deflection direction of the wind direction under the Coriolis force. In the Northern Hemisphere, wind direction deflects to the right; in the Southern Hemisphere, wind direction deflects to the left. Figure ④ fits the combination of wind belts near 60° in the Northern Hemisphere, so it should be 60°N; Figure ③ fits the combination of wind belts near 30° in the Northern Hemisphere, so it should be 30°N; Figure ① fits the combination of wind belts near 30° in the Southern Hemisphere, so it should be 30°S; Figure ② fits the combination of wind belts near 60° in the Southern Hemisphere, so it should be 60°S. Therefore, the order from north to south is 60°N, 30°N, 30°S, 60°S, corresponding to the numbers ④③①②.
